title: Fate Marable, Bill Johnson and the California union
summary: Talk of Marable, Bill Johnson's trip to California and union rules there.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: I just wondered if I ever heard you, maybe didn't know you in the old days. Faith Malibu. Yeah. Faith Malibu, he's one of the fellow. There's another Faith, too, that's in California.
You might have met him, a tall, light fellow, played trombone.

I've heard that name. Faith, what is his name? I don't know whether he's going to see. Somebody played with... He played with Bill Johnson in them, too. I think he's played with Ice Can Tate, too. He played with Bill Johnson in them out there, I think, too. Really? I've never met him. Bill Johnson's been to California again, they tell me. I haven't seen Bill Johnson in the middle. Is he back now? Yeah, he's back now. I haven't got to see. He said a man can't get a job in California if he don't belong to that union. Yeah, that's true. He can't get a job. He can wait a while. Yeah, make you wait a while. You've got to be there a year before you can get a job, see? I told him, I said, you'll probably go to California and let him figure on going to work, and then after you get there a while, make yourself acquainted and then, you know, stay around. Yeah, so, yeah. Well, I'm surprised we were here about Eddie Gallen. I didn't know that. Yeah? I had to scrap with the oldie. And he's not hard to get along with, I don't believe. Oh, yeah. Everybody I know likes him.
